spans.text: The 2-s instruction period and 4-s rating period were modeled with a canonical hemodynamic response function at the onset of each period; the 10-s regulation period and 4-s relaxation period were modeled as a boxcar regressor convolved with the canonical hemodynamic response.

model_settings.value: Participant-level fixed effects were modeled using a mixed design in SPM99; a general linear model produced participant contrast images that were entered into group SPM{t} analyses. Instruction and rating periods were modeled with canonical HRF regressors, while regulation and relaxation periods were modeled as boxcar regressors convolved with the canonical HRF.

description.value: Functional images were slice-time corrected and motion corrected using SPM99, anatomical images were coregistered and normalized to a standard template, functional images were normalized using those parameters and interpolated to 2 × 2 × 2 mm voxels, smoothed with a 6 mm FWHM Gaussian filter, and high-pass filtered with a 120 s cutoff.

spans.text: Functional images were slice time corrected and motion corrected using SPM99 (Wellcome Department of Cognitive Neurology). Anatomical images were coregistered to the mean functional image and normalized to a standard template brain; the functional images were then normalized using those parameters and interpolated to 2 × 2 × 2 mm voxels. Functional images were smoothed with a Gaussian filter (6 mm full width-half maximum). A high-pass filter with a cutoff period of 120 s was applied to remove drifts within sessions.
